coverage_note: Read the full transcript end-to-end. Logged only corrections where Amal’s voiced response clearly signals a fix (and a single tier-3 English insertion: “white”). Skipped many teaching-only stretches and several ambiguous moments (e.g., dish-name back-and-forths and some “last/end” phrasing where the exact Arabic preposition in Amal’s line wasn’t fully recoverable). Also didn’t log most English-only segments (Halloween summary, meta English about English grammar) and focused vocab-audit mainly on cases with clear spoken correction or clear tier-3 English drop-in.

rows.amal_said: What does alta'at take؟ There is two options.
rows.why: Amal asked what التقيت takes; after the prompt Medi added مع (…التقيت مع… خطيبتي) and Amal accepted.
Medi said “three years” (ثلاث سنين) but Amal corrected to the dual form “two years” (سنتين).
Amal corrected the gender/form from feminine حلوة to masculine حلو.

rows.medi_said: What do they call the big... the bread with the things in the middle?
rows.why: Medi asked for the name of the filled pastry; Amal supplied the Arabic word معمول.
rows.english: name of the filled pastry with something in the middle

rows.why: Medi only said “لأول”; Amal clarified the intended phrase for “for the first time” as “La awal mara” (أول مرة structure).

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة نص كم. white
rows.why: Medi inserted the English word “white” inside an Arabic sentence; the sheet has “white (m/f) | Abyad | أبيض | abyad”.

rows.medi_said: You can't say هذي، هذا واحد؟
rows.amal_said: No, we would just say هذي or this.
rows.why: Amal rejected the mixed demonstratives and instructed to use only the gender-matched pair هذي/هذا.
Amal distinguished that خايف describes the scared person, pushing toward the verb-based adjective; after that prompt Medi produced بخوّف and Amal confirmed.

rows.amal_said: No, the be goes before the s.
rows.why: Amal corrected the present-verb prefix: present verbs should start with b- (يبسط, not يسبط).

rows.amal_said: So no preposition needed. 'Cause it makes them happy.
rows.why: Amal said that with the causative meaning (it makes them happy) you don’t use a preposition after بيبسط.

rows.proposed_rule: Adjective number agreement: when the noun is plural (e.g., أواعي/هدول أواعي), use a plural adjective (المفضلين) not a singular adjective (مفضلة).
rows.why: Amal recast singular mفضلة to the plural form مفضلين to match the plural noun (my mom’s favorite clothes).

rows.amal_said: آخر الطريق would suffice, yeah. If you wanna say على، you can also say it.
rows.proposed_rule: For “at the end of + place/thing”, Arabic can use the fixed pattern “آخر + noun” without needing “في”; “على” can also be used as an alternative.
rows.why: Amal said that the phrase without the preposition “في” is sufficient: “آخر الطريق”.
rows.english: at the end of the road
